title: The Impact of Managerial Ownership on Acquisition Attempts and Target Shareholder Wealth

rival_explanations: managerial entrenchment (CEOs reward themselves after thwarting the bid)
equity/severance awarded to place the CEO in a stronger bargaining position to attract better future takeover bids
reverse causality: incentives raised to motivate the CEO to search for more favorable future bids rather than to improve performance

context.industry_setting: cross-industry (U.S. publicly traded takeover targets; no industry concentration, top failing sectors business services, utilities, pharmaceuticals)
context.sample_description: 178 unsuccessful takeover targets (received by 169 firms) identified from the SDC U.S. Mergers and Acquisitions Database (transactions not labeled completed, deal value >= US$1 million), merged with COMPUSTAT, CRSP, and Standard and Poor's ExecuComp; missing compensation collected from proxy statements and 10-K forms on EDGAR

data_sources.name: CRSP (Center for Research in Security Prices)
proxy statements and 10-K forms on EDGAR (compensation and severance data collected manually for non-ExecuComp firms)
hand-collected internal governance data from proxy statements (board size, board independence, board meetings, governance committee, large shareholders, CEO duality)

analyses.label: Table 1: Unsuccessful takeover sample distribution, failure reasons, trading status, and CEO turnover (Panel E compares forced CEO turnover vs rejection/subsequent acquisition)
analyses.sample: 178 unsuccessful takeover bids received by 169 targets, 1994-2011

dv.name: target outcome / CEO turnover
dv.measure: trading status (remain independent / acquired / delisted) 3 years after bid; total and forced CEO turnover within 2 years after bid withdrawal

key_ivs.name: forced CEO turnover
key_ivs.measure: forced CEO departure within 2 years of bid withdrawal, cross-tabulated with target rejection and subsequent acquisition

analyses.label: Table 2: Descriptive statistics of firm characteristics and CEO compensation, year TA-1 vs year TW+2 (univariate before-after)

dv.name: firm characteristics and CEO compensation
dv.measure: median MV equity, MV assets, book assets, M/B, sales, leverage, ROA, sales growth, RETURN, market-adjusted RETURN, Cash Pay, Equity Pay, Total Pay, Equity ratio, and severance/parachute figures at year TA-1 and year TW+2, in constant 2011 dollars

key_ivs.name: bid failure (before vs after)
key_ivs.measure: comparison of year TA-1 (pre-announcement) vs year TW+2 (post-withdrawal) medians

analyses.label: Table 3: CEO compensation comparison - unsuccessful targets vs industry/size/performance-matched control firms vs matched successful targets (difference-in-difference)
analyses.sample: 178 unsuccessful targets, 178 matched control firms, 178 matched successful targets, 1994-2011

dv.name: CEO compensation (Total Pay and Equity Pay)
dv.measure: median Raw Total Pay (Panel A) and Equity Pay (Panel B) at TA-1 and TW+2 with percentage change and z-statistics, constant 2011 dollars

key_ivs.name: unsuccessful takeover attempt (treatment vs control)
key_ivs.measure: unsuccessful takeover targets vs industry-, size-, and performance-matched control firms (no takeover), before-vs-after change

analyses.label: Table 4, Specification (1): CEO post-bid compensation change on pre-bid abnormal compensation (Eq. 1, OLS)

key_ivs.name: pre-bid abnormal compensation (ACOMP)
key_ivs.measure: residual from COMP = a0 + a1*Size + a2*(Ri-Rm) + a3*ROA + a4*Age + a5*Industry + a6*Year, estimated over all ExecuComp firms 1994-2011

analyses.label: Table 4, Specification (2): ex post settling-up difference-in-difference with matched control firms (Eq. 1)
analyses.sample: 178 unsuccessful targets + 178 matched control firms (356 obs)

key_ivs.name: ACOMP
key_ivs.measure: CEO pre-bid abnormal compensation (residual)

key_ivs.name: ACOMP x Control
key_ivs.measure: interaction of ACOMP with Control dummy (=1 for matched control firm, 0 otherwise)

key_ivs.name: AFTER x ROA
key_ivs.measure: interaction of AFTER with ROA - change in PPS after bids

key_ivs.name: AFTER

analyses.label: Table 5, Specification (4): CEO PPS difference-in-differences, unsuccessful targets vs matched control firms (Eq. 2)

analyses.label: Table 7: Post-bid CEO compensation change on pre-bid abnormal compensation moderated by internal governance (Eq. 1 with governance proxy, OLS)

analyses.label: Table 9, Panels A-B: internal governance quality and long-term abnormal performance across three response groups (univariate)
analyses.sample: 178 unsuccessful takeover targets (Group1 N=41, Group2 N=69, Group3 N=68)

dv.name: governance mechanisms and abnormal performance
dv.measure: median board size, board independence, governance index (Panel A); median abnormal operating cash flow (AOCF) and abnormal stock return (ARETURN) from year T-1 to T+3, abnormal = target minus industry- and size-matched control firm (Panel B), with Wilcoxon z-statistics across groups

key_ivs.name: target response group (G1/G2/G3)
key_ivs.measure: Group 1 = independent with comp change below median (N=41); Group 2 = independent with comp change at/above median (N=69); Group 3 = acquired or delisted within 3 years (N=68)

analyses.label: Table 9, Panel C: regression of long-term performance change on response-group dummies (Eq. 3)

dv.name: performance change (delta AOCF / delta ARETURN)
dv.measure: change in abnormal operating cash flow (delta AOCF) and change in abnormal stock return (delta ARETURN) from year T-1 to T+3; abnormal = target minus industry- and size-matched control firm's OCF/return

key_ivs.name: G1 / G2 (response-group dummies)
key_ivs.measure: G1 =1 if target belongs to Group 1 (independent, low comp change), 0 otherwise; G2 =1 if Group 2 (independent, high comp change), 0 otherwise

analyses.label: Alternative explanations (supplementary appendix): subsample comparisons of compensation change by financial-leverage change (102 increase vs 76 decrease) and by CEO turnover (132 no-turnover vs 46 turnover)
analyses.sample: 178 unsuccessful takeover targets split into subsamples

dv.name: CEO compensation change
dv.measure: median (and abnormal) CEO compensation change from year TA-1 to TW+2 with z-statistics, compared across subsamples

key_ivs.name: post-bid leverage change / CEO turnover
key_ivs.measure: leverage increase vs decrease subsamples; CEO-turnover vs no-turnover subsamples

proposed_edge.from: weak-governance firms do not react properly
